chunks: My father narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī al-Za‘farānī, who said: Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr al-Aslamī narrated to me, who said: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Anbasah narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Amr, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbās, who said:

The angel who came to Muḥammad (peace be upon him) informing him of the killing of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was Jibra‘īl (peace be upon him), the Trustworthy Spirit, with his wings spread out, crying and screaming. He had carried some of the dust of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), and it emitted a fragrance like musk. The Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him) said: 'Will my nation achieve salvation when they kill my chick?' Or he said: 'the chick of my daughter.' Jibra‘īl replied: 'Allāh will afflict them with discord, so their hearts will disagree with one another.'

key_terms.فَرْخُ ابْنَتِي: The chick of my daughter (metaphor for al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What did the angel Jibra‘īl bring to the Prophet to inform him of al-Husayn's martyrdom?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn ‘Abbās describes Jibra‘īl bringing fragrant dust from al-Ḥusayn’s grave to the Prophet, symbolizing the physical reality of the martyrdom even before its occurrence. The Prophet’s query regarding the 'success' of the ummah highlights the paradox of spiritual triumph through sacrifice, while Jibra‘īl’s response identifies internal division (*ikhtilāf*) as the divine consequence for the killers. This event underscores the Shia theological view that the tragedy of Karbala is not merely historical but a pivotal cosmic event with immediate theological repercussions for the Muslim community.
